GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: The skill's doctrine comes from the owner's prompting guide (external, v3.1) distilled into self-contained English rules, plus two backported pieces: pointer craft from public agent-instructions guidance and the enhancer-boundary from this repository's own agent set. Three product decisions shape the spec. First, consumer-safe language: bundled-skill consumers know nothing about GRACE, so shipped content names only user-visible vvoc artifacts (enhancer task XML, .vvoc spec/plan identity conventions, vv-handoff) and describes the unique-identity doctrine as enforced by vvoc tooling there and as a strong default elsewhere — replacing the reviewed draft's GRACE house-law framing. Second, bounded volume: the reviewed draft (~540 lines) exceeded every non-system house skill and the craft etalon vv-design-principles (436 total), so the spec fixes 80/4/420 line budgets, funded by removing GRACE internals, section-number provenance, three unsourced figures, and paragraph-length boundaries. Third, boundaries kept but terse: ownership rules are load-bearing (the skill must not fork the enhancer schema or own the spec/plan lifecycle), so they compress to at most six one-line scope rules instead of disappearing. The substantive core the spec preserves from the reviewed draft: compilation doctrine (classification, conflict scoping, minimal sufficient specification, ambiguity policy), the action-versus-topic negation distinction, structure and addressability (unique identities vs stable types, wrapped pasted content, tokenizer checks), session update semantics (extends/supersedes/preserves/removes, state vs history, Q-IDs, readback, resume brief), evidence levels, and the controlled evaluation protocol. The one deliberate regression fixed by backport is pointer craft, which the draft dropped and which matters directly for managed-skill descriptions.

Alternatives.Alternative: Ship the reviewed draft as-is: rejected — ~540 lines against the 436-line etalon, GRACE-internal terminology invisible to consumers, section references into a guide consumers do not have, and three quantitative claims without checkable sources.
Bundle the prompting guide as a fifth reference: rejected — 78 KB would roughly triple the skill's volume and lock shipped content to a machine-local Russian document.

Remove the boundaries section entirely: rejected — without ownership rules the skill invites forking the enhancer schema and duplicating vv-spec/vv-plan lifecycle duties; the cost of keeping them is six one-line rules.

Keep GRACE phrasing and teach consumers the internal conventions: rejected — the skill's audience is every vvoc user, not contributors to osovv repositories; internal conventions add tokens and confusion without changing behavior for them.

A merged single-reference skill with no session guidance: rejected — session-state failures (stale requirements, bare external results) are the primary observed pain in vv-opencode workloads; dropping them removes the skill's differentiator versus public alternatives.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Exact wording, section order, and which contract rules stay in the core versus moving to references (implementation-plan decisions under AC-03 and AC-14).
Whether pointer craft earns a place in the SKILL.md core or stays a reference section — start in references; promote only if the manual evaluation shows routing failures.
Whether the optional title-level credit line ships and in what wording (implementation decision under AC-12).
Whether a repeatable manual-eval runbook later moves to docs/ — only if the practice recurs after this change.

Scenarios.Scenario: A raw mixed request ("look at it, do it properly, briefly, and do not touch X") compiles into a sufficient specification: deliverable named, conflict scoped (deep analysis, bounded report), preserve list explicit, non-goal preventing the likely drift.

A mid-session requirement change arrives as "now do it differently, but keep the rest": expressed through supersedes naming the replaced rule ID and preserves listing the surviving IDs, without rewriting history silently.
An external query returns empty: the result is wrapped with its Q-ID and an explicit empty status, so a later reference treats absence as a fact rather than re-querying blindly.
A delegation prompt needs a single-task XML: the skill emits the enhancer schema with its field names rather than inventing a parallel schema.
A skill description fires on the wrong tasks: rewritten pointer-first with one trigger per branch and collapsed synonyms, then checked on the intended and neighbor tasks.
A pasted chat log enters a prompt: wrapped in a paired tag with provenance, so its markup cannot bleed into instructions and later references resolve exactly.
